content: Honest extraction-failure UX pattern (from Readwise Parsing FAQ): Readwise explicitly states 'we'll never be able to parse 100% of the internet 100% perfectly. HTML and CSS are just too flexible.' Surface design: (1) browser extension positioned as 'an exception handler' for when server-side URL fetch fails/mis-extracts - because it gets the rendered DOM, not the naked URL; (2) 'Report document parsing issue' feedback channel on every document; (3) when a highlight position cannot be matched with sufficient confidence between original-web and Reader-app, the app 'will notify you that it failed to match and those highlights will still be visible in the Notebook tab' - never silently re-attach and never silently drop; (4) de-duplication is URL-exact only, content-level de-dup is documented as unsupported. Implication for Lem Reader (already has DOC-06 disclosure spirit + ANNO-07 tri-state annotation resolution): ingestion MUST surface 'this URL could not be reliably read' rather than silently producing a near-empty article; partial extraction should be flagged; the v1.0 ANNO-07 ambiguous/orphan resolution model extends naturally to anchor mismatches between extraction and re-render.
